results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 63 aligned outline summaries match their spec paragraphs' controlling ideas in spec order, including the in-practice order now chronological (record, rings Oct 2027, replay Nov 2027, branch sample Q2 2028, Polish vehicles); the five callout units carry the thesis_statement and roadmap callouts. Covers AC-3.

Four units were marked two_ideas (Scene ¶2, Scene ¶4, Architecture ¶13, In Practice ¶2); each joins exactly what its spec paragraph's controlling idea joins (p07 late rule + no Motorvane link; p09 inventory incl. each brand's arrangement; p37 rings vs flags + group-urgent classes; p44 the two contested decisions).
Every unit carries its spec paragraph's contribution to S1-S6; none is off-thesis.

Figures 1-6 (Figure 3's layers and tenancy services are now named in the prose), the terms, isolation, platform-model, ladder, decision-record, trade-off and vertical tables, the quotations (Adevinta 2019, AVIV 2021/2025, Adevinta dispute back office, OLX Hydra, Vinted, eBay 2013) and the 300-branch statistic are each introduced and their point stated in the prose.

All other paragraph, section and conclusion transitions express their declared relationship and pick up the declared known information (e.g. 'Ingrid's question starts with words', 'Sharing beneath products needs a tenancy model', 'The first tenancy service, the tenant register', 'Veldmark's tests showed its decisions working for one group', 'The limits just described fall hardest on real estate', 'Decisions prevent those failures', 'Those drills matter because', 'These questions test those decisions').

results.draft_locus: Architecture: A Tenancy Model for a Marketplace Group ¶16
results.quote: Multi-region deployment is a separate decision.
results.finding: Declared contrast carrying over the boundaries between tenants' data and introducing whether data spans regions at all; the sentence names neither the two boundaries just described nor the region question, and the subsection lead ('Two boundaries limit what tenants share') announced only two topics, so the paragraph reads as an unannounced third topic (both flow readers stumbled here).

results.draft_locus: In Practice: Veldmark's Tenancy Model v1 ¶7
results.quote: The Polish vehicles section, where both brands operate, shows how the layers combine.
results.finding: Declared example carrying over the branch classification (values to configuration, behavior to extensions) and introducing one market where all mechanisms meet; the opening does not pick up the classification, and the paragraph sits under the 'Configuration replacing branches' subheading without any link to branches, so both flow readers found it out of place.

results.quote: Without a tenancy model, eight failures recur.
results.finding: Declared contrast carrying over 'where sharing fits each vertical'; the opening does not refer to the verticals or to sharing's fit at all (flow reader B: 'no bridging sentence connects them').

Both readers describe problem -> vocabulary -> options -> design -> application -> evaluation, matching the spec's prerequisite_order with problem_solution and grouping; no section's position was unclear to either reader and neither would change the top-level order. Excluded: both readers paused at 'The Category Straitjacket' / 'Billing by Guesswork' and reader B at 'Daan Visser', but these are on audience.already_knows (earlier chapters), so they are not counted.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: One Rule, Four Countries, Three Days ¶4
results.quote: Keybridge, the agency software business, is a SaaS company with its own customers, not a marketplace; it also serves Hearthly's competitors, so Veldmark committed in March 2027 not to use its data for Hearthly.
results.finding: Both readers: the Keybridge commitment interrupts the tenant count and pays off only at decision 3. The spec's evidence asks only that Keybridge be noted as a SaaS company, not a marketplace; the March 2027 commitment clause is the draft's addition and can move to decision 3 or be explained.

results.finding: Both readers: the sentence says every model combines global components and configuration, but the first models in the table (fork per country, federation) use neither; reword so the six models are ways of sharing more or less (from nothing to the whole product).

Owned terms (tenant, tenancy model, global component, configuration over code, isolation tiers, tenancy services, register, hierarchy incl. 'seller segment (such as professional sellers)', extension points, ladder, rings, group-urgent classes, exit paths, integration principal now glossed as 'an outside system's login', BCP 47, ISO 4217, CLDR, GDPR Chapter V, DSA, VIN) are defined at or before first substantive use; failure-pattern names and the Veldmark cast are on already_knows. No reader reported an unexplained term outside already_knows.
Opens on a direct statement of cost (ten copies pay ten times), then the opposite failure; none of the weak patterns.
Conclusion answers the opening question and hands off by contrast; no bare restatement, new material or 'in conclusion'.

'a value lives in configuration, a behavior in an extension point, a fork under an expiry date and a fraud rule in a group-urgent lane, all resting on a tenant code carried everywhere and an exit path per tenant' with so-what 'Improvements are bought once; markets stay local.'
Calls back to Ingrid's question and the 7 March rule: 'the 7 March rule reaches every tenant at once, not Belgium three days late'.

The cold reader predicted the subject (sharing without forcing one product; tenant first-class; configuration over code with the configure-extend-fork limit; share beneath the product, uniform and pooled first), the section order (phishing scene, terms, six platform models, tenancy model, Veldmark's version, trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, questions) and the evidence (Adevinta, eCG, OLX, AVIV, Vinted, locale/currency standards, EU law, fictional Veldmark), matching the roadmap and AC-2's expected. Its only friction (the six models not yet named) is not a misprediction.

The answer names brand x country tenants with codes in every identifier, event and log; fraud rules as a group-urgent class bypassing rings; the group detector plus tenant locale packs in a 48-hour shadow window; the shared hashed block list as the cross-brand trust signal; and answers the brand with decision 5's scope (configuration service mandatory only for global components, the brand keeps its own configuration and uses the group service where it consumes a group capability). Matches AC-1's expected.
